learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Entry checks are low stakes; a missed fresh re-entry returns control without exit credit.

items.title: Starting check: attitude or action
items.prompt: A student reports privately believing that members of another group are less trustworthy, but no behavior is described. Which construct is directly supported?
options: Institutional discrimination
Individual discrimination
Prejudice
Equal-status contact
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: person-level action
items.prompt: A landlord personally refuses to show an available apartment to a qualified applicant because of the applicant's social-group membership. Which classification best fits the described mechanism?
options: Prejudice only, because behavior is irrelevant
Individual discrimination
Institutional discrimination through a standing rule
A neutral outcome with no group-linked treatment
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: rule-level mechanism
items.prompt: A company automatically rejects applications from a recurring list of neighborhoods, and the rule systematically excludes one social group from consideration. Which mechanism is most directly described?
options: Institutional discrimination via a recurring rule
Only a private prejudice with no action
An isolated interpersonal disagreement
A stereotype with no allocation consequence
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: avoid intent inference
items.prompt: A hospital scheduling routine repeatedly assigns fewer desirable shifts to one group, but the vignette gives no evidence about any scheduler's private beliefs. Which conclusion is best bounded by the evidence?
options: Every scheduler is prejudiced
No discrimination can occur without stated prejudice
The pattern proves a legal violation
Institutional mechanism; attitude unknown
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: three-part classification
items.prompt: A supervisor expresses a negative group attitude, then personally denies one worker training because of group membership; no standing policy is involved. Which combined classification is supported?
options: Prejudice plus individual discrimination
Institutional discrimination only
Prejudice without discriminatory action
Institutional discrimination plus a legal finding
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: choose mechanism evidence
items.prompt: A school shows a persistent group difference in access to advanced courses, but the cause is unspecified. Which additional observation would most directly support an institutional-discrimination classification?
options: One student reports feeling disappointed
A recurring placement rule systematically screens the group out
A teacher privately holds a negative attitude but never makes placement decisions
The groups have different average course preferences
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: use the two-axis matrix
items.prompt: Which sequence best classifies a vignette?
options: Infer intent, then decide legality, then identify behavior
Classify attitude/action, then person/routine
Start from group outcome and assume prejudice
Treat every stereotype as an institutional rule
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: clinic assignment
items.prompt: A clinic director personally assigns fewer leadership opportunities to qualified staff from one group because of their group identity, while no clinic-wide rule is described. Which classification fits?
options: Institutional discrimination from a standing rule
Prejudice only with no action
Individual discrimination
A neutral institutional routine
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: identify mechanism evidence
items.prompt: Which observation best distinguishes institutional discrimination from an unexplained group disparity?
options: The disparity is statistically visible
A group member reports low confidence
A repeated group-linked allocation rule
One observer dislikes the outcome
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: grant allocation
items.prompt: A foundation's awards show a group disparity. Which new fact most directly supports an institutional mechanism rather than one reviewer's isolated choice?
options: A shared scoring rule discounts group experience
One rejected applicant believes the process was unfair
One reviewer expresses a private stereotype but did not score applications
Award recipients celebrate their results
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Starting check: identify power
items.prompt: A department chair can set hiring criteria and approve every final offer. Which enabling concept is most directly represented?
options: Formal power over decisions
Prestige without authority
A private stereotype only
Class consciousness
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Guided practice: identify prestige
items.prompt: An organization routinely accepts recommendations from a highly honored professional group even though that group has no formal hiring authority. Which mechanism is most direct?
options: Formal coercive power
Prestige-based influence
A legal mandate
Mechanical class mobility
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Less help: identify class-linked access
items.prompt: Unpaid internships are the main route to a profession, and only applicants with substantial financial support can accept them. Which mechanism is most directly described?
options: Class-linked resources shaping access
Prejudice proven in every supervisor
Prestige caused by a formal title
Individual discrimination by one named actor
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: On your own: require action evidence
items.prompt: A group has high prestige in an institution, but no differential treatment or allocation is described. What can be concluded?
options: Institutional discrimination is proven
Prejudice is proven
Prestige, not discrimination
Legal equality is proven
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Near exit: trace institutionalization
items.prompt: Senior partners control promotion rules, treat referrals from a prestigious network as more credible, and encode that preference into a recurring promotion criterion that disadvantages workers outside class-linked networks. Which explanation best fits?
options: Power encodes prestige and class access in an institutional rule
Prestige alone proves every partner holds prejudice
Class position directly determines ability without an institutional gate
The recurring rule is individual discrimination only
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Changed exit: break the institutional channel
items.prompt: A causal model shows an unmeasured private attitude and an organization-wide discretionary scoring rule that produces discrimination. Which modeled change removes the institutional channel without asserting attitude change?
options: Remove recurring rule; attitude unknown
Assume the manager no longer holds the attitude
Increase the manager's prestige
Rename the scoring rule without changing how it allocates opportunities
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: build the causal chain
items.prompt: Which sequence is best supported for explaining facilitation of discrimination?
options: Group disparity → assume prejudice → declare legal result
Resource/status → gate influence → differential allocation
Class label → fixed personal ability → outcome
Prestige → automatic institutional discrimination with no action
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh near re-entry: research funding
items.prompt: A high-prestige committee influences which topics are considered credible; executives with budget power turn its preferences into a recurring funding rule that excludes researchers lacking elite class-linked networks. Which mechanism is supported?
options: Prestige shapes credibility; power encodes; class shapes access
Class proves the excluded researchers lack ability
Only individual prejudice is possible because people wrote the rule
No discrimination can be institutional when prestige is involved
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Repair: locate institutionalization
items.prompt: Which change marks movement from an isolated discretionary act to institutionalization?
options: The actor thinks about the decision longer
The action enters a recurring organizational rule
The affected person disagrees
The actor gains a private preference
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry: admissions routine
items.prompt: A dean once favored applicants from a prestigious club. Later, the school embeds club membership as a recurring admissions bonus. Which observation most directly identifies the changed institutional mechanism?
options: The dean's private attitude is now legally proven
The club becomes less prestigious
A recurring admissions rule carries the preference
Every applicant acquires equal class resources
items.directions: Choose one response, then commit it to receive feedback.
